no_setting.says: 1Password's privacy policy lists software errors and crash data among what it collects, and documents no setting to turn that off.

settings.note: It is off unless you chose to share, and it is set for each account.
settings.steps: select your account at the top of the sidebar, then Manage Accounts, the account, Usage data, and deselect Share information about your usage

no_setting.says: Arc's security page describes its telemetry and crash reports and documents no setting to turn them off.

settings.note: It is on by default. Builds from F-Droid do not show the switch.
settings.steps: Settings > About, then turn off Submit crash logs
Settings > Privacy and Security, then turn off Automatically send completely private product analytics to Brave and Automatically send daily usage ping to Brave

settings.note: An older Brave page calls this switch Help improve Brave's features and performance.
settings.steps: Settings > Privacy and Security > Data Collection, then turn off Automatically send diagnostic reports to Brave

no_setting.says: OpenAI's privacy policy lists usage and log data among what it collects and documents no setting in the app to turn that off. Its setting to stop your chats being used to improve the model is about training, not about this.

settings.note: Google says these reports can include personal information, and that a crash report can hold memory from the crash, such as page contents, payment information and passwords.
settings.steps: More > Settings > You and Google > Google services, then turn off Help improve Chrome's features and performance
More > Settings > Google Services, then turn off Help improve Chrome's features and performance

no_setting.says: Anthropic documents switches for the app's crash reports and product analytics only as managed settings for administrators, not as a setting in the app. Its setting Settings > Privacy > Help improve our AI models is about training on your chats, not about this.

settings.note: The app describes it as sharing anonymized crash and usage data. It is on by default and the change takes effect the next time cmux starts.
settings.steps: Settings > App, then turn off Send anonymous telemetry

no_setting.says: Cursor documents no setting for its usage analytics or crash reports. Its Privacy Mode (Cursor Settings > General > Privacy Mode) is about training AI models on your code, not about these.

Dia's privacy policy says it collects data on which features you use automatically, and documents no setting to turn that off. Its setting Settings > Privacy > Share content data to help improve Dia is about the content you browse, not about this.

settings.note: Discord says the app keeps sending the data and Discord stops using it for this purpose. The setting is for your account, on every device.
settings.steps: User Settings > Data & Privacy, then turn off Use Data to Improve Discord

settings.note: Discord says the app keeps sending the data and Discord stops using it for this purpose. The setting is for your account, on every device.
settings.steps: Settings > Data & Privacy, then turn off Use Data to Improve Discord

settings.note: Docker describes this one switch as covering diagnostics, crash reports and usage data. It is on by default, and an administrator can lock it.
settings.steps: Settings > General, then turn off Send usage statistics

settings.note: Edge always sends its required diagnostic data: this switch is for the optional data. Your organization can manage it.
settings.steps: Settings and more > Settings > Privacy, search, and services > Privacy, then turn off Send optional diagnostic data to improve Microsoft products

no_setting.says: Figma documents no setting in its apps for usage analytics or crash reports. Its cookie choices are for its website, and it says they do not work in its mobile apps.

settings.note: These settings apply to every Firefox profile on this device.
settings.steps: Settings > Privacy and security > Firefox data collection and use, then turn off Send technical and interaction data to Mozilla and Send daily usage ping to Mozilla
Settings > Privacy and security > Firefox data collection and use, then turn off Automatically send crash reports
GitHub Desktop > Settings > Advanced, then under Usage turn off Help GitHub Desktop improve by submitting usage stats

settings.note: It is on by default. In the app's code the switch stops usage analytics at once, and crash reports from the next time Logseq starts.
settings.steps: Settings > Advanced, then turn off Send usage data and diagnostics to Logseq

settings.note: Notion's cookie notice puts Cookie settings under My notifications & settings, which the app now calls Settings > Preferences. Notion says the cookie settings cover its desktop apps.
settings.steps: Settings, then Cookie settings, and turn off analytics cookies
Settings > App settings > General, then under Application turn off Send anonymous usage data to Postman

settings.note: Proton describes this one switch as covering usage statistics and crash reports. It is on by default.
settings.steps: Preferences > Advanced, then turn off Share anonymous usage statistics

no_setting.says: Raycast says it saves usage statistics and error reports to fix bugs and improve the app, and documents no setting to turn that off.
Screen Studio sends crash reports automatically. Only a team admin can turn them off, for the whole team.

settings.steps: Settings > Usage data: off

no_setting.says: Slack's privacy policy lists device and crash data among what it collects and documents no setting in the app to turn that off. Its cookie settings are for its website.

settings.note: Trezor says this switch also stops its automatic error reports. An error that happens before Suite has loaded your choice is still reported, with less detail.
settings.steps: Settings > Application, then turn off Anonymous data collection

alternatives.about: the same editor, built from the same open source code without Microsoft's telemetry
alternatives.name: VSCodium

settings.note: Extensions you installed may collect usage data of their own, which this setting does not cover.
settings.steps: open Settings (⌘,), search for telemetry.telemetryLevel and set it to off

settings.note: Warp says this stops its product analytics and the content it collects to improve the service, unless your organization's settings enforce them.
settings.steps: Settings > Privacy, then turn off Help improve Warp
Settings > Privacy, then turn off Send crash reports, a switch of its own

settings.note: What Zed's servers record for its hosted AI and collaboration features is needed for those features, and no setting covers it.
settings.steps: open Settings (⌘,) and search for telemetry, then turn off diagnostics (crash reports) and metrics (usage data); in the settings file that is "telemetry": { "diagnostics": false, "metrics": false }

settings.note: It is a setting of your Zoom account, and an account admin can lock it.
settings.steps: sign in to the Zoom web portal, not the app: Profile > Data and Privacy > Data settings, then turn off Optional Diagnostic Data
